This series never disappoints. There is nothing quite as satisfying as a long distance sniper kill! The graphics are great. The music alone make this so cinematic! The game play can get your heart pumping. it's  perfect mix of action and strategy. 
Fun game to play, highly recommend!

ive broken so many hearts with my sniper rifle

I loved the previous Sniper Elite games , playing through them in co-op was superb. This one however just feels a bit of a let down.

The main problems seem to be :

- take-downs often just don't work , even with 2 people trying to take down the same enemy in co-op. The enemies will often stop just out of range and see you before you can activate the take down which is not a problem that I noticed in the previous S.E. games where they were far more reliable and made stealth much more fun as it felt like your own fault when you messed up , whereas in this game it feels more like the game is at fault and frequently ruins your stealth attacks with methods that would have been reliable in the previous games.

- enemies often just return to their on patrol state even when things are exploding and gunfights are going on nearby , it seems to follow no obvious logic - sometimes they are alerted way across the map, other times they're close by and totally ignore all the noise.

- enemies seem to get stuck behind scenery - found this a few times where an alerted enemy would later be found still alerted stuck behind a crate or something just walking / running on the spot trying to get through the obstacle.

- there seems to be nothing new in the skill tree, just the same stuff as before. It would have been nice to have a few new skills to use. Same items too as before. Some new guns but nothing that feels like anything more than just more of the same.

All in all it feels a bit of a let down. It's fun to play in co-op but the issues with the takedowns have really spoiled it and the lack of anything new is making it a bit of a chore to play through the final few missions, and much more often we've just ended up blasting everything in sight after yet another failed takedown that really should have worked.

I'd still recommend it but be aware that it feels more like a DLC pack than a properly new game.
Good game, nice gameplay like in Sniper Elite 4
Adding another entry to the Sniper Elite series, it is fun.

After playing literally every game in the series within a month or two (winter sale bundle) people saying this isn't like the old games are high off their ass. It's 5 but with different maps and weapons. not a bad purchase, I'm not even using the dlc weapons because the base game ones fit my style more. 

If you liked past entries or want to get right into a game, get it. Still have collectibles and some upgrade stations to get, haven't even touched then game outside of campaign and only have 13 hours.

Wait for a sale if you're really on the fence. Didn't feel bad about full price since I just played every game at a steep discount. The devs do a great job of a pretty optimized game in 2025, very few bugs if any.

When a game is truly great, I don't understand all the complaints of "it's more of the same".  To me, that is a GREAT thing!  When a game is good, I DO want more of the same, and Sniper Elite: Resistance delivers that.  The maps are NOT the same, only the game-play style is identical - and that's fine by me.

SE: R had a rocky release so it did catch some negativity for that, but it's a great game, though bugs still persist with sticking on stairs, a silenced pistol having the gunshot bang of a loud rifle....  They're not game-stopping bugs though, and Rebellion does tend to fix their stuff in a reasonable time-frame.

I have close on 50 hours in a first play-through (I typically spend twice as long in a game as the average player.  There are some great opportunities for sniping in this title with some terrifically long-distance shots to be had.  There is a better variety of maps than in SE: 5 - some great set pieces. The maps vary in size too.  They all LOOK huge, but some are much, much smaller than they look at first glance, but otherwise, I'm finding the game is really enjoyable and am looking forward to another replay to find some of the collectables I missed first time.

I don't play Invasion and I don't give a fig about the new timed challenges added (nice touch for people who want this but, for me, it breaks immersion completely so I won't be playing these - I'd sooner that development time was dedicated to more of the campaign instead of these add-ons).  The story of Kleine Blume is brilliant and this creates a good tie in for the gameplay.  SE: R has continued the same workbench upgrade mechanics (excellent), and the same skill points can be earned (these I find totally underwhelming to be honest and barely bother using them). 

The protagonist, Harry Hawker, I'm not at all keen on, especially the voice acting. But his chatter was culled somewhat in an update and he's now a less grating character.  It is a nice spin-off to play another protagonist and I could see this being a neat way forward for Rebellion - to have different protagonists involved in different areas of the same resistance fighting.

All in all, a pretty good game - and I look forward (hopefully) to a SE: 6 entry soon.
Highly recommended for those folks who prefers a chill way to snipe your enemies. Got me hooked on the first run and the additional modes brought more fun with extra challenges.
